To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The reaction mechanism of the selective catalysis reduction (SCR) on vanadium-based SCR catalysts relies on the involvement of Lewis acid sites, which are vanadyl groups (VO) on the vanadium oxide surface; (2) The SCR reaction is a two-step process: (i) NH3 reacts with the Lewis site to form a nitrosamide intermediate, and then (ii) the nitrosamide reacts with NO to form N2.
the SCR reaction on V2 O5 -TiO2 catalysts is a redox process, which proceeds on Lewis sites.
the Lewis site is the active site of SCR and that the nitrosamide is an intermediate in the SCR reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the chemical reactions that are relevant to energy and environmental issues.
understanding the chemical reactions of technological interest, such as selective catalytic reduction of nitric oxide, using operando spectroscopy and transient perturbations.
the development of novel catalysts and catalyst systems, the elucidation of their structure–activity relations, and the elucidation of reaction mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Lewis sites on V2 O5 -TiO2 are the active sites in SCR.
the SCR reaction proceeds through a mechanism involving Lewis acid sites.
the SCR mechanism is not as complex as it was thought to be, and the reaction is not as sensitive as previously believed to the nature of the acid site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reaction mechanism of SCR on V2 O5 -TiO2 is not the same as that on the industrial V2 O5 /TiO2, but that the mechanism on V2 O 5 -WO3-TiO2 is the same as that of V2 O5-TiO2.
the SCR of nitric oxide by ammonia on vanadia on titania (V2O5-TiO2) is a surface redox reaction involving Lewis acid sites.
the SCR mechanism of NOx over vanadia based catalyst is not a simple Brønsted acid catalyzed reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reaction mechanisms of SCR are not only governed by the redox properties of the catalyst but also by the nature of the active sites, namely, Lewis or Brønsted acid sites.
